question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[\frac{1}{2},\frac{9}{2}],$ compute $P(X\ge 1).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[\frac{1}{2},\frac{9}{2}],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4},\, & \frac{1}{2}\le x\le \frac{9}{2}, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 1) & =P(1\le X\le \frac{9}{2}) \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{9/2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{9/2}\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(\frac{9}{2}-1)}{4} \\  & =\frac{7}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
